chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him),

regarding two men who both killed one man. He said: 'If the guardians of the killed one intend to kill both of them, they must pay a complete blood money and kill both of them, and the blood money will be divided among the guardians of the two who were executed. If they intend to kill only one of the two and kill him, the one left must pay half the blood money to the family of the killed one. And if they do not demand blood money from either of them and do not kill either of them, the guardian of the killed one may accept the blood money from both of them.'

key_terms.أولياء المقتول: The next-of-kin (guardians/heirs) of the murdered person, who hold the right to demand qisas or diya in Shia jurisprudence
key_terms.الدية: Diya — the blood money or wergild paid as financial compensation for unlawful killing; a full diya is the standard unit
key_terms.القتل: Qatl — homicide/killing; in jurisprudential context refers to the act requiring either retaliation (qisas) or compensation (diya)
key_terms.المتروك: Al-matruk — 'the one left behind,' i.e., the surviving killer not executed, who bears ongoing financial liability
key_terms.كليهما: Both of them — emphasizing joint liability of both killers

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling when two people jointly commit a murder, according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses the jurisprudential ruling when two men jointly commit a murder together. The ruling provides three options to the victim's next-of-kin (awliya'): (1) execute both killers after paying each a full diya, which is then distributed among the families of those executed; (2) execute only one, while the surviving killer pays half the diya; or (3) waive execution entirely and accept diya payments from both. This ruling reflects the classical Islamic principle that the right to qisas (retaliation) belongs to the victim's family, not the state, and that financial compensation must accompany any exercise of retaliation when multiple killers share responsibility.
